expectations.text: Distinguishes between possible CAUSES of the drop-off before proposing fixes, rather than going straight to an idea list
expectations.evidence: Opens by rejecting the friction framing, then '## First: split the 60%' with four distinct causes — 'Never received it / Received but never opened / Opened but didn't complete / Never got that far' — plus two diagnostics (median time-to-verify, resend rate) BEFORE the '## Ideas' section.

expectations.text: Raises that the 60% may be composed of different populations, or may be partly a measurement or attribution artifact
expectations.evidence: 'If you added verification to stop fraud, part of that 60% may be bots doing exactly what you wanted. Real drop-off and fake drop-off look identical in the aggregate funnel.'

expectations.text: Does not re-propose shortening the form or adding a progress bar
expectations.evidence: Neither is re-proposed; the progress bar is argued against — 'a progress bar tells people how much work is left, not why to do it.' ('ask whether you need [the phone number] at signup at all' is step elimination, not form shortening.)

expectations.text: At least one option questions whether verification needs to happen at that point in the flow at all
expectations.evidence: 'Delete or defer the step (biggest lever, usually) — Let people into the product unverified, in a limited state, and verify at the first moment it actually matters.'

expectations.text: Options differ in mechanism (channel, timing, who verifies, whether to verify) rather than in copy, layout, or visual design
expectations.evidence: Group-level axes are mechanisms: defer/delete the step, SSO (who verifies), magic link, provider failover and SMS fallback (channel), polling/state-restoring links (device continuity), resume emails (timing). A minority of bullets are copy/template ('Trust and motivation' section, plain-text emails), but they are not the axis of variation.

expectations.text: Handles the ambiguity in 'account-verification' — either asks which kind, or states which reading it assumed and what would change under the others
expectations.evidence: Never addresses which kind of verification. It assumes email/SMS OTP throughout (SPF/DKIM, subject-line codes, one-time-code autofill) with no stated assumption. The closing question asks 'why do you verify at that point — regulatory, fraud, deliverability ... or just convention?' — which is a why question, not the which-kind ambiguity.

expectations.text: Proportionate to a bounded product question: under roughly 1200 words, no ceremonial section headings with no content under them
expectations.evidence: wc -w = 806 words, comfortably under ~1200. Five headed sections, all with substantive content; no empty ceremonial headings.
